Need to rewrite this in PyTorch from scratch with proper streaming."
> — posted by Łukasz Kowalski (U_LUKAS), ts=1706110000.000100, channel C03IJKL9012 (#engineering)

I verified this was the only message in the channel carrying a 👀 reaction from the AI teammate (I also checked a "thumbsup" reaction from the bot and an "eyes" reaction from a different human user, ruling those out).

However, I was unable to actually delete this message. Every `chat.delete` attempt (tried with different encodings, with `as_user=true`, and with an explicit `user` param) returned:
`{"ok":false,"error":"cant_delete_message"}`

I confirmed via `chat.update` tests that this is a permissions issue, not a bad timestamp: the authenticated identity (bot user U01AGENBOT9, is_admin=false, is_owner=false) can only modify/delete messages it authored itself. Since this message was authored by a different (human) user, Slack's permission model blocks deletion by this bot token — there is no admin-level override available with the current credentials/API access.

**Result:** Correct target message identified, but deletion could not be executed due to insufficient permissions on the authenticated bot account. Completing this would require an admin/owner-level user token (e.g., Robert Walsh or Morgan Freeman, both flagged `is_admin:true` in this workspace) to delete another user's message.
